identity.real_world_identity_notes: Classic Mini Cooper S of 1965, classed by AMS2 under Vintage Cars Tier 2. AMS2 also carries this car under Copa Classic B as a separate entry, curated as mini-cooper-s-1965-b; the two are kept as separate records by reviewer decision rather than sharing one. Its four-speed gearbox is the three-synchromesh type fitted to all Minis between 1959 and 1968.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.
The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional for that reason.
First gear has no synchroniser on the three-synchromesh box fitted until September 1968, so a downshift into first needs the driver to match revs. The other three gears are synchronised.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mini-cooper-s-1965.20260817t193016084z-732907cf by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Controls observed live with automatic clutch and shifting disabled; the gearbox is established by a marque specialist covering the classic Mini's boxes from 1959 to 1968.

claims.basis: Marque-specialist history of the classic Mini gearbox, matched to the exact observed AMS2 telemetry identity.

The specialist source records the three-synchromesh gearbox fitted to every Mini until September 1968, with synchronisers on second, third and fourth and none on first. The guided drive selected four forward gears through an H-pattern gate.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. A guided drive settles it, by holding the throttle through an upshift and seeing whether the gear engages.

driver_summary: Three-synchromesh gearbox: second, third and fourth have synchronisers and first does not, on every Mini until September 1968. Blip to ease the synchronised gears, and match revs yourself for any downshift into first.
